text: What was done and when, latest first.

The statement on candidates in Prop. 5.7 now has an elementary proof: every candidate has $|\Phi(Q)|\ge16$, i.e. rank $\le\log_2|Q|-4$. The classification of the groups of order $2^9$ and rank $8$ and the computation of their descendants are no longer needed (they remain as checks). Lean proves that no candidate has $|P_2(Q)|\le8$, and also proves Lemma 5.6. Consequence: a counterexample of order $2^{12}$, if any, has rank $\le8$.

Lean: Jennings' theorem in the case needed — $D_5(Q)\le Q\cap(1+\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}(Q)^5)\le Q^8\gamma_2^4\gamma_3^2$ for finite $2$-groups of class $\le3$ (via the Jennings basis and the Lazard series); Lemma 5.2(a)–(c) given $D_3=\gamma_3$; the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7 given $D_3=\gamma_3$ and Prop. 5.3.

The Lean formalization has been ported to Lean/Mathlib v4.35.0 with the module system and submitted to the Palomar registry: nine theorems (Theorems 6.6 and 6.8, Lemma 5.6, the two statements of Prop. 5.7 on candidates, Jennings' inclusion, and three conditional ones: Prop. 2.1, Lemma 5.2(a)–(c), the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7); the mechanical check passed and the automated (AI) review found no blocking problem; registered as PALOMAR-2026-10-23-000007.

Certificates for Prop. 5.3: each of the $3400$ groups of order $2^{10}$, given by its pc presentation, comes with a finite module and matrices; Lean checks the relations, that all products of four $(g-1)$ vanish, and faithfulness, hence $D_4=D_5=1$ and order $2^{10}$. The $3400$ checks run as compiled code (native_decide), not in the kernel; the soundness of the checker (a passing check gives a faithful representation killing $\Delta^4$) is proved in Lean and kernel-checked. The completeness of the list is Lemma 5.2(d) and the ANUPQ computation. Data and scripts.

Lean: Theorem 6.10 ($P^{*\prime\prime}=1$; for every central extension by a subgroup of exponent $p$, since Mathlib has no $p$-covering group), Remark 2.2, Lemma 5.2(d) (a minimal counterexample is an immediate descendant of step size $1$) and Lemma 6.9 (the filter on parents). The remaining paper results and the classical hypotheses ($D_3=\gamma_3$, the theorems of Passi and Gruenberg) are next in the formalization plan.
The preprint is submitted to arXiv (math.GR).

An exact criterion for nonterminality of $p$-groups of type $(d,2,1)$ (Theorem 6.12): proved on paper for odd $p$ and elementary $P/\gamma_2$, checked by computer at $3^8$, $3^7$, $5^7$, $7^7$. The question is removed from the open ones.
In the paper: an explicit Lie algebra of type $(3,3,1,1)$ with $[M_2,M_2]\ne0$ over $\mathbb F_p$ for every odd $p$ (Appendix A); the full case $a=2$ of Theorem 6.8 (Appendix B).

A repeat with ANUPQ with the audit fixes: the $2^{10}$ search (all $858$ chunks, $3400$ candidates and the lattice answers) and ranks $2$–$4$, $7$, $8$ of order $2^{11}$ agree exactly with the old runs. The caveat on orders $2^{10}$ and $2^{11}$ is lifted.
$2^{11}$, rank $5$: $824$ candidates, all with $D_4=D_5=1$ (about $83$ CPU-hours, part of them on BOINC). Order $2^{11}$ is settled: a counterexample, if any, has order $\ge2^{12}$ (Prop. 5.10).

Lean: Tahara's Theorem 6.1 (the description of $D_5$ for finite groups of class $\le4$) is proved in Lean, with no sorry and only the standard axioms; Theorems 6.6 and 6.8 are now proved in Lean with no hypotheses. The formalization found a typo in our transcription of Tahara's condition (C₂); it was fixed before the proof.
$2^{11}$, rank $6$: $13$ candidates, all with $D_4=D_5=1$.
On paper: $D_5=\gamma_5$ when $Q/\gamma_2$ has at most one invariant larger than $3$ (including $C_9\times C_3^{s-1}$); an independent review found no errors.
References: what Tahara actually announced (p. 173), and the search for his separate paper.
Computer check for $C_9\times C_3^{s-1}$ and $C_{27},C_{81}\times C_3^{s-1}$: $2\,057$ groups, $4\,537$ elements $z$, none in $D_5$.
ANUPQ audit (ispacex.github.io/gap): the $3^9$ descendant step was repeated with the fixed version, and the result is byte-identical.

On paper: $D_n(H\circ E)=D_n(H)$ for central products with $D_8$, $Q_8$ and $M_{2^{k+2}}$ (adjoining a central square root); all $386$ candidates of orders $2^6$–$2^9$ satisfy the conditions. Two independent reviews.

On paper: gluing along a proper subgroup of $Z(E)$ — a lemma on central roots of any degree (Lemma 5.9). The splittings of the $386$ candidates: $20$ split, each has a splitting covered by Prop. 5.8. An independent review and a recount by another method.
Lean: Lemma 5.9 (a central root of any degree) is proved in Lean, with no sorry and only the standard axioms; formalizing the other paper results has started.

Lean: Prop. 5.8 is proved in Lean in all cases ($D_8$, $Q_8$, $M_{2^{k+2}}$), with the ring statement $\mathbb Z[H]\cap\Delta(Q)^n=\Delta(H)^n$; $Q_8$ and $M_{2^{k+2}}$ reduce to $D_8$ through one overgroup $(Q\times\mathbb Z)/\langle(s,-2)\rangle$.

Lean: the reduction (Prop. 2.1, Remark 2.3) is proved modulo explicit hypotheses — the theorems of Passi and Gruenberg and $D_3=\gamma_3$: from class $\le3$ to finitely generated groups and to finite $2$-groups of class $3$; for finite groups Gruenberg's theorem is not needed.

Lean: Lemma 6.3 and Prop. 6.5 ($[\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\subseteq\gamma_5$; a non-metabelian $p$-group of class $4$ and rank $d$ has order $\ge p^{d+5}$) are proved in Lean with no hypotheses; instead of the Lie ring, the group $G/\gamma_5$ and the Hall–Witt identity.

Lean: Theorems 6.6 and 6.8 ($D_5=\gamma_5$ for $G/\gamma_2\cong C_{3^a}\times C_3^{s-1}$) are proved in Lean modulo Tahara's Theorem 6.1, stated as an explicit hypothesis and checked against the scan; both subcases, including the row $s$ of condition (E).
The group analogue of Theorem C: $D_7=1$ for the plateau group; the first search at $c=4$; at $c=5$, $D_7\ne1$ but $D_8\cap\gamma_5=1$.
Order $3^8$: the full scan, $904$ non-metabelian groups, $D_5=1$ in all.
Order $3^9$: the $p$-cover filter, $62\,245$ candidates, $D_5=1$ in all; rank $5$ excluded on paper.
On paper: $D_5=\gamma_5$ for $Q/\gamma_2$ of exponent $3$; the Lie-ring lemma; $P^{*\prime\prime}=1$. Two independent line-by-line reviews.
Order $2^{10}$ closed: the minimal-counterexample lemma, ANUPQ, $3400$ candidates.
Lossless pruning of the $2$-group tree for $2^{11}$; ranks $2$–$3$ and $\ge8$ closed.
$2^{11}$, rank $4$: $52\,568$ candidates, all with $D_4=D_5=1$.
$2^{11}$, rank $7$: the step-$2$ descendants of $(\mathbb Z/2)^7$ taken from SmallGroups ($1\,112$ groups); $9$ candidates, all with $D_4=D_5=1$.
